entities.summary: Anna of Hohenstaufen, born Constance, was an Empress of Nicaea, daughter of Frederick II, Holy Roman Emperor and Bianca Lancia. She played a crucial role in the Byzantine Empire's politics during the 13th century, navigating the complexities of imperial succession and religious conflicts. Her influence extended to the Crusades, with her husband, Baldwin II of Constantinople, participating in the Fourth Crusade. Anna's legacy as a regent and diplomat has been studied by historians, who note her efforts to maintain stability in a region ravaged by war. The Hohenstaufen dynasty's decline, partly due to Anna's family's involvement in the Fourth Crusade, marked a turning point in the history of the Byzantine Empire. The impact of Anna's actions can still be seen in the modern-day politics of the Eastern Mediterranean.
